apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Design
metadata:
  id: default
  title: A parcel locker
spec:
  description: |
    **A worked example, small enough to read in one sitting.**

    Three blocks, one flow, one saved request and one suite — a person
    drops a parcel into a locker and the ledger learns about it.

    Nothing here is a real system. What is real is the *shape*: every file in
    this design is byte-for-byte what the emitter renders, which is what makes
    the directory usable as a fixture as well as an example.
  board:
    links:
      calls:
        color: "#7d8794"
        dashed: false
      related:
        color: "#a1668a"
        dashed: true
  implementation:
    root: .
---

apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Adr
metadata:
  id: ADR-001
  title: The ledger is a file, not a database
spec:
  state:
    status: decided
  decided: 2026-03-02
  source:
    where:
      - test/fixtures/design/README.md#the-ledger
  description: |
    One locker bank writes a few hundred rows a day. A file that can be read
    with `less` beats a database nobody has credentials for at 3am, and the
    append-only rule is enforced by the filesystem rather than by a trigger
    somebody can drop.
---

metadata:

  title: Sequences written on one line
  tags: [edge, hand-written]

    role: handler
  source:

apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2

metadata:
  id: CMP-INTERIOR-COMMENT
  title: A comment in the middle of the document
spec:
  place:
    group: GRP-CORE
    # Whether this is a module or a boundary is the open question, and the
    # comment saying so is halfway down the file.
    role: handler
  state:
    status: open
---
apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Block
metadata:
  id: CMP-KIOSK
  title: The kiosk
  tags:
    - edge
    - touched-by-a-person
spec:
  place:
    group: GRP-EDGE
    role: adapter
  state:
    status: decided
  code:
    service: locker.kiosk
    implements: kiosk/main.go
  source:
    where:
      - test/fixtures/design/README.md#the-edge
  description: |
    The only block a person touches. It knows a door number and a parcel
    barcode, and nothing else — no addresses, no names, no ledger.

    🟢 That narrowness is the point: the kiosk is the block most likely to
    be replaced, and the one with least to carry over when it is.
---
apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Block
metadata:
  id: CMP-LEDGER
  title: The ledger
  tags:
    - append-only
spec:
  place:
    group: GRP-CORE
    role: handler
  state:
    status: decided
  code:
    service: locker.ledger
    implements: internal/ledger/log.go#Log
  description: |
    Append-only. A parcel that went in and never came out is a row that has no
    partner, and finding those is the whole reason the ledger exists rather
    than a `parcels` table with a `collected` column.
---
apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Block
metadata:
  id: CMP-LOCKS
  title: The lock controller
spec:
  place:
    group: GRP-CORE
    role: handler
  state:
    status: open
  code:
    service: locker.locks
    implements: internal/locks/controller.go#Controller
  description: |
    Opens one door at a time and refuses to open a second while the first is
    still ajar.

    The refusal is the interesting half. A door that will not open is a
    complaint somebody makes; a bank of doors all open at once is a story in
    the local paper.
---
apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Block
metadata:
  id: "CMP-QUOTED-ANYWAY"
  title: "Quoted where nothing needed quoting"
spec:
  place:
    group: "GRP-CORE"
    role: "handler"
  state:
    status: "decided"
---
apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Contradiction
metadata:
  id: CTR-001
  title: "*Doors are dumb* (the controller decides) vs *doors are smart* (each door holds its own timer)"
spec:
  state:
    status: open
    severity: blocker
  description: |
    Two designs for the same hardware. Which one is true decides whether
    `CMP-LOCKS` is a service or a router.

# One flow: what happens between a person and a ledger row.
#
# `before` is the state each block is in when the flow starts, and the
# `components` map on a step is what that step changed. A step that changes
# nothing says nothing.

apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Flow
metadata:
  id: drop-a-parcel
  title: Drop a parcel
spec:
  entry:
    method: POST
    path: /v1/parcels
  before:
    CMP-LOCKS:
      doors.open: 0
    CMP-LEDGER:
      rows: 0
  steps:
    - id: person
      at: CMP-KIOSK
      phase: caller
      label: Somebody scans a barcode
      note: The only actor. Everything after this is the locker answering one question — which door.
    - id: pick
      at: CMP-LOCKS
      phase: execute
      label: Choose a free door
      budgetMs: 50
      components:
        CMP-LOCKS:
          doors.open: 1
      findings:
        RSK-001: The step that picks one door is the step a fail-open would turn into all of them.
    - id: write
      at: CMP-LEDGER
      phase: execute
      label: Append the row
      budgetMs: 10
      components:
        CMP-LEDGER:
          rows: 1
      note: "Written before the door opens: a row with no parcel behind it is recoverable, a parcel with no row is not."
    - id: open
      at: CMP-LOCKS
      phase: return
      label: The door opens
---

apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Open
metadata:
  id: OPN-001
  title: "Who owns a parcel nobody collects: the sender or the locker?"
  tags:
    - custody
spec:
  state:
    status: open
  source:
    where:
      - test/fixtures/design/README.md#custody
  description: |
    Blocks 🔵 `QST-001`, because the answer decides who the ledger is written
    for.
---
apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Question
metadata:
  id: QST-001
  title: How long is a door held before the parcel is called abandoned?
  tags:
    - custody
    - policy
spec:
  state:
    status: open
  answered: 2026-04-12
  holdDays: 7
  slaLabel: "72"
  description: |
    **Recommendation:** seven days, then the parcel moves to the depot and the
    door frees. Not a technical number — a contractual one — so it belongs in
    `design.yml`, not in `internal/locks`.
---
# One saved request. The filename is its id.
#
# A scenario, not a measurement — everything here is designed data.

apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Request
metadata:
  id: drop
  title: Drop a parcel
spec:
  type:
    capability: parcels
    delivery: unary
    version: v1
  initial:
    method: POST
    path: /v1/parcels
    header.authorization: Bearer lk_kiosk_…
    state: received
  group: parcels
  send:
    path: /v1/parcels
    method: POST
    body:
      barcode: "0007734"
      bank: north-street
      note: "left of the bike rack "
---
apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Risk
metadata:
  id: RSK-001
  title: '**Open-on-failure** applied to the lock bank = "every door open at 3am"'
  tags:
    - safety
spec:
  state:
    status: open
    severity: critical
  reviewed: false
  description: |
    Fail-open is right for the display and wrong for the doors, and the two
    live in one binary today.
---
apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Suggestion
metadata:
  id: SUG-001
  title: Write the ledger before the kiosk, not after
  tags:
    - sequencing
spec:
  state:
    status: open
    severity: major
  description: |
    Everything else can be re-run from an append-only log. Nothing can be
    re-run from a kiosk.
---
apiVersion: elderlygate/designer/design/v2
kind: Suite
metadata:
  id: a-full-bank-refuses
  title: A full bank refuses rather than picking a door twice
spec:
  note: Three drops against a bank of two. The third is the test; the first two only get it there.
  steps:
    - request: drop
      expect:
        - status: 201
    - request: drop
      expect:
        - status: 201
    - request: drop
      expect:
        - status: 409
        - spans.absent: locker.ledger
